name: India: Kashmir, Manipur and the Maoist belt

status.en: 268 armed incidents reported in the past seven days, 34% fewer than the week before, most of them in Delhi, Mumbai and Hyderabad.
status.nb: 268 væpnede hendelser meldt de siste sju dagene, 34 prosent færre enn uken før, flest i Delhi, Mumbai og Hyderabad.

summary.en: Violent clashes between Kuki and Naga groups in Manipur have escalated, with Kuki volunteers shot dead and five Kuki men found mutilated in gunny bags, prompting protests in Kangpokpi and Noney and police tear-gas and baton responses. In Chhattisgarh, security forces recovered arms, explosives and Maoist communication equipment from a forest dump in Kanker, indicating ongoing anti-Maoist operations. A road accident in Reasi, Jammu and Kashmir killed one person and injured two. The conflict now combines ethnic violence in Manipur, Maoist security actions in Chhattisgarh, and a separate accident in Kashmir, while 437 battle-related deaths were recorded in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Voldelige sammenstøt mellom Kuki- og Naga-gruppene i Manipur har eskalert, med Kuki-frivillige skutt død og fem Kuki-menn funnet lemlestet i jutesekker, noe som har ført til protester i Kangpokpi og Noney og politi som har brukt tåregass og batonger. I Chhattisgarh har sikkerhetsstyrker funnet våpen, sprengstoff og maoistisk kommunikasjonsutstyr i en skogavfall i Kanker, noe som indikerer pågående anti-maoist-operasjoner. En veitrafikkulykke i Reasi, Jammu og Kashmir drepte én person og såret to. Konflikten kombinerer nå etnisk vold i Manipur, maoistisk sikkerhetsaksjon i Chhattisgarh og en separat ulykke i Kashmir, mens 437 dødsfall knyttet til kamp ble registrert i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: Kashmir conflict
background.extract: The Kashmir conflict is a territorial conflict over the Kashmir region, primarily between India and Pakistan, and also between China and India in the northeastern portion of the region. The conflict started after the partition of India in 1947 as both India and Pakistan claimed the entirety of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir. It is a dispute over the region that escalated into three wars between India and Pakistan and several other armed skirmishes. India controls approximately 55% of the land area of the region that includes Jammu, the Kashmir Valley, most of Ladakh, the Siachen Glacier, and 70% of its population; Pakistan controls approximately 30% of the land area that includes Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan; and China controls the remaining 15% of the land area that includes the Aksai Chin region, the mostly uninhabited Trans-Karakoram Tract, and part of the Demchok sector.
